title: iTantra -Indian Multilingual TTS & STT Aided Neural Transceiver Radio Access for low bitrate links
department: Department of Space / Indian Space Research Organisation
description:
Background As vocal audio information is very data intensive making it difficult to transmit through low data rate links. In alert and distress based scenarios Transmitting Audio information is critical instead of written message as it will be more inclusive and will cater to everyone even if they are literate or not.
Description Build an Android App with lightweight, highly accurate STT and TTS models for 10 Indian Languages (Hindi, Gujarati, Marathi, Kannada, Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, Odia, Bengali, English) that runs locally on a low-power device. The system’s STT module when activated after detecting pauses and stoppages should form the sentences detected and must instantly and efficiently stream the data through wifi/Bluetooth connected embedded device or another phone with same application with minimal latency. The systems TTS module when activated after receiving the Text data should convert it into intelligible speech which will be played as a voice note and alert type messages will be announced at highest volume non-interruptible. To verify the complete loop two phones with same app one in TTS mode and another in STT mode can be connected via wifi or Bluetooth and it should work like a walkie talkie using push to talk feature, if turned off it should work like a phone.
Key Metrics for Evaluation
• Efficiency: Model size, App size (RAM/Flash footprint) and CPU usage during idle listening. (20%)
• Accuracy: Low Word Error Rate for STT and High human legibility and flow for TTS. (40%)
• Latency: The Time delay between the Words said and STT completion, Time delay between the text received and audio processed and played for TTS along with RTF (Real Time Factor). The time delta between the sentence said and the same sentence started as audio in another phone. (20%)
Software & Framework Restrictions
• Open-Source Only: The use of proprietary, closed-source, or commercial voice-activation SDKs is strictly prohibited.
• Allowed Frameworks: Teams must build their pipelines using open-source machine learning and TinyML frameworks. Recommended tools include TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers, PyTorch Mobile or similar.
• Fully Offline Working: Model or pipeline should work fully offline only and no internet hosted API based solutions are expected and encouraged for the STT or TTS.
Expected Solution Teams are expected to deliver a robust, deployable system architecture. A successful submission must strictly satisfy the following technical boundaries:
• Hardware & Runtime Environment: The Android application must run smoothly on Low and Mid rage mobile phones.
summary: Innovation (4/5): draws on machine learning, neural applied to a miscellaneous problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Miscellaneous. Tech Depth (5/5): centers on api, model, architecture. Sustainability (4/5): has a clear long-term maintenance path. Scalability (3/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 21/30 -> Green verdict.

detail.title: iTantra -Indian Multilingual TTS & STT Aided Neural Transceiver Radio Access for low bitrate links

overview.in_plain_terms: Build an app that turns speech into text on one phone, sends just that text over a slow Bluetooth or wifi link, and turns it back into spoken audio on the other phone, basically a walkie-talkie that transmits words instead of raw audio, in 10 Indian languages.
overview.why_it_matters: Raw voice audio is data-heavy and unreliable over weak or low-bandwidth links, exactly the conditions you get in disaster and alert scenarios. Sending text instead of audio makes the message get through reliably, and converting it back to speech at the other end means it works for people who can't read.
pain_points: Voice is too data-heavy to transmit reliably over low-bitrate emergency links, but text-only alerts exclude anyone who can't read.
Ten Indian languages means ten separate STT and TTS pipelines that all have to run locally, on-device, with no cloud dependency.
The system has to behave like a real walkie-talkie (push-to-talk) and also as a normal phone when toggled off, that's two different interaction modes in one app.
overview.background: Vocal audio is very data-intensive, making it hard to transmit over low-data-rate links. In alert and distress scenarios, transmitting audio matters more than a written message, because it's more inclusive and reaches people regardless of literacy.
overview.whats_being_asked: An Android app with lightweight, accurate STT and TTS models for 10 Indian languages that runs fully on-device: one phone's STT converts speech to text and streams it over wifi/Bluetooth, the other phone's TTS converts that text back into spoken audio, working as a push-to-talk walkie-talkie between two devices.
expected_solution: On-device STT that detects speech pauses/stoppages, forms sentences, and streams the text with minimal latency over wifi/Bluetooth.
On-device TTS that converts received text into intelligible speech, played as a voice note, with alert-type messages announced at max volume, non-interruptible.
Full loop demo: two phones, one in STT mode, one in TTS mode, connected via wifi/Bluetooth, working like a walkie-talkie with push-to-talk.
Toggled off, the app behaves like a normal phone (not stuck in walkie-talkie mode).
Support for 10 languages: Hindi, Gujarati, Marathi, Kannada, Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, Odia, Bengali, English.
Open-source-only frameworks, no proprietary voice SDKs.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Breakthrough band. The clever part isn't STT or TTS individually, both are known problems, it's using text as the transmission medium to solve a bandwidth problem, then closing the loop back to speech so literacy isn't a barrier. That reframing of 'voice over a bad link' as 'text-relay with voice bookends' is the genuinely inventive move.
analysis.invention_effort_note: High. Ten languages times two model types (STT+TTS) is real breadth, even if you scope down to 2-3 languages for the demo, the architecture has to be built to plausibly extend to all ten.

competitive_landscape.note: Multilingual voice-AI PS types are common at SIH, but the specific 'text-as-transport-layer walkie-talkie' framing is unusual, most teams will default to a generic translation-app pitch and miss the low-bitrate transmission angle, which is actually the core ask.

innovation.note: Reframing voice transmission as text-relay for bandwidth-constrained links is a genuinely non-obvious systems idea, not just a translation-app wrapper.

invention.note: Ten-language STT+TTS, a Bluetooth/wifi transport layer, and a dual-mode UI (walkie-talkie vs phone) is a lot of surface area for 36 hours.

technical_feasibility.note: On-device, open-source-only STT/TTS for 10 Indian languages at low latency is genuinely hard, pick 2-3 languages with the best open-model support and be upfront that's your demo scope.

impact_and_benefits.note: In alert/distress scenarios, a reliable low-bandwidth voice relay that's inclusive of non-readers has an obvious, defensible real-world use case.

architecture.note: STT -> text transport -> TTS is a clean three-stage pipeline, the main integration risk is the two-device sync, not the individual models.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick if the team scopes language coverage honestly, 2-3 languages done well beats 10 done badly. The core pipeline (STT -> transport -> TTS) is straightforward to demo convincingly once built, and the low-bitrate framing gives you a clear judge-facing story that most competing 'voice AI' pitches won't have.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: The two-phone walkie-talkie demo is inherently visual and convincing, judges can watch someone speak into phone A and hear phone B talk back, in real time, no explanation needed.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Chasing all 10 languages evenly will likely mean none of them work reliably, pick your best-supported 2-3 languages (Hindi + English + one more with strong open STT/TTS model support) and be explicit that's the demo scope.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Confirm hour 0: which of the 10 languages have solid open-source STT and TTS model availability (check Coqui, IndicTTS, AI4Bharat resources)? Build your language priority list around what actually has usable open models today.

idea_0_4: Pick 2-3 target languages based on open-source model availability (Hindi + English are safest bets, add one more Indic language with strong AI4Bharat/Coqui support).
Sketch the transport protocol: how text gets packaged and sent over Bluetooth/wifi between two phones, decide this before writing app code.
Split ownership: one person on STT pipeline, one on TTS pipeline, one on the Android app shell and transport layer, from hour 0.
prototype_4_22: Get STT working standalone first: speech in, text out, for your chosen languages, verify accuracy before touching the network layer.
Get TTS working standalone: text in, spoken audio out, verify intelligibility before integration.
Build the Bluetooth/wifi transport connecting two phone instances, test with hardcoded text first, then wire in live STT output.
integration_22_30: Connect the full loop: phone A speaks -> STT -> text sent -> phone B receives -> TTS speaks it, test end to end repeatedly.
Implement push-to-talk toggle and the 'normal phone mode when off' behavior, this is an explicit requirement, don't skip it.
Add the non-interruptible max-volume alert-message mode as a distinct message type from regular conversation.
polish_30_36: Rehearse the live two-phone demo until the handoff is smooth, this is your single most convincing moment, protect it.
Prepare a clear one-slide explanation of why text-relay solves the low-bitrate problem better than raw audio compression, that's your core technical argument.
Have a fallback recorded demo video in case live wifi/Bluetooth is flaky in the venue.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Lead the demo with the actual walkie-talkie exchange between two phones, live, before explaining any architecture. Let the judges hear it work first, then explain why it's the right approach for low-bitrate emergency links.

strengths: The core pipeline directly matches a real, well-articulated problem (bandwidth-constrained emergency voice comms).
A live two-device demo is highly visual and doesn't need much explanation to land.
weaknesses: Ten-language scope is unrealistic for 36 hours, requires honest, upfront descoping.
Two-device Bluetooth/wifi demos are notoriously flaky at hackathon venues with heavy wifi congestion.

roles_needed: Someone fluent in at least one target Indic language for accuracy testing
team_fit.ideal_ratio: Roughly even split across the three roles, this PS has no single dominant bottleneck, STT, TTS, and transport all need real attention.
team_fit.approach: Build STT and TTS as independent, testable modules in parallel from hour 0, only wire them into the live two-phone transport once each is individually verified working.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Android app scaffolding, Bluetooth/wifi socket boilerplate, and wiring up existing open-source STT/TTS model APIs can be AI-assisted quickly.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Actual speech intelligibility and accuracy in the target Indic languages needs a native or fluent speaker listening and correcting, AI transcription tools can be confidently wrong on Indic language nuance.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: If nobody on the team actually speaks the target language well enough to judge STT/TTS quality, you risk demoing a pipeline that sounds fine to you but is actually garbled or wrong to a native speaker, judges may include one.

data_resource_availability.status: Open-source STT/TTS model support varies significantly by language, Hindi and English have strong open options; some of the 10 listed languages (Odia, for instance) have thinner open-model coverage.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: If a chosen language's open models underperform, fall back to demoing that language in a degraded 'best effort' mode while your primary 2 languages carry the live demo.

judge_qna.question: Why send text instead of just compressing the audio?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Text is orders of magnitude smaller than even heavily compressed audio, which matters directly on the low-bitrate links this PS targets, and it degrades gracefully instead of becoming garbled audio.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's your measured bandwidth savings versus a compressed-audio baseline?

judge_qna.question: How do you handle STT errors, since a misheard word changes the whole message?
judge_qna.strong_answer: We show the transcribed text on-screen before it's sent for alert-type messages, so there's a confirmation step, and we're honest that free-flowing conversation mode accepts more risk of transcription error.
judge_qna.follow_up: For a genuine distress alert, would you want a confirmation step, or does that cost too much time?

judge_qna.question: Why only 2-3 languages in the demo when the brief asks for 10?
judge_qna.strong_answer: We prioritized languages with strong open-source model support to guarantee real accuracy in the time available, and our architecture is built so adding a language means swapping in new model weights, not rewriting the pipeline.
judge_qna.follow_up: Walk us through exactly what changes when you add an 11th language.
